title: Clarify affordances for compound-icon and split-action buttons across themes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Several regressions and inconsistent affordances have emerged for compound (icon + label) buttons and split-action patterns across light/dark/high-contrast themes. Observed issues include: inconsistent spinner placement for loading states, unclear disabled styling in high-contrast, hitbox shrink on compact icon+label combos, and mismatched token values after the recent semantic token migration. Goal: define a small, prescriptive set of visual & interaction rules that cover: 1) primary/secondary/ghost variants when an icon is present, 2) loading and disabled states (spinner placement, accessible status announcement, preserved width), 3) split-action (primary + dropdown) affordances, and 4) theme token overrides for high-contrast and dark modes. Deliverables: updated token table, Figma components and variants, interaction spec (hover/focus/active/loading/disabled), and a short dev spec to unblock ENG-4021 for implementation and regression fixes.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Kickoff: scoped to compound and split-action patterns only; standalone icon-only work tracked separately.

2025-02-14 — Design exploration: produced 3 approaches for spinner placement (prefix, inline, overlay). Team prefers prefix spinner to avoid layout shift but keep option for overlay on small icon-only buttons.
2025-02-20 — PM feedback (Ethan Liu): prioritize accessibility announcements for loading states (aria-live polite) and preserve button width during loading to avoid layout reflow.

2025-02-25 — Engineering sync (ENG-4021 owner): kernel for token migration will change base background tokens; we need a clear mapping for high-contrast overrides. ENG requests exact token names and fallback values.

2025-03-01 — Design review: consensus on token names, spinner prefix for compound buttons, overlay for icon-only compact variant, and an explicit disabled contrast recipe for high-contrast theme. Rohan to update Figma and add dev spec.
2025-03-02 — Attached PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7142 (WIP) — contains style token mapping and initial CSS vars for dark/high-contrast.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens: explicit mapping table for primary/secondary/ghost variants that includes light, dark, and high-contrast overrides
Figma: components with documented variants for icon-left, icon-right, icon-only compact, and split-action with dropdown visual states
Interactions: documented loading strategy (prefix spinner for compound; overlay for icon-only compact) with aria-live guidance and preserved width behavior
Accessibility: disabled contrast meets AA or higher for high-contrast theme; keyboard focus and hitbox parity verified
Engineering handoff: dev spec with token names, CSS var examples, and a regression checklist provided to ENG-4021
